originalTitle: US stocks: S&P 500 ends higher as CoreWeave results fuel AI optimism
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news: The US stock market had a good day on Wednesday, with many stocks going up in value. This was partly because some companies that work with artificial intelligence (AI) had strong earnings reports, which made investors more optimistic about the future of AI. These good reports also helped other related companies, like those that make computer chips, do well in the market. As a result, investors now think it's more likely (62% chance) that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates the same next month, which is good news for the market. This matters because steady interest rates can help the stock market continue to grow and do well.

originalTitle: US Treasuries hold gains as softer inflation weakens rate-hike fears
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the value of US government bonds (called US Treasuries) is going up because inflation (the rate at which prices are rising) is not as high as people thought it would be. This means that investors are less worried that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates soon. As a result, people are more interested in buying US government bonds, which is why their value is increasing. The government recently sold some of these bonds to investors, and the sale was successful, showing that investors are still interested in buying them. This matters because it shows that investors are feeling a bit more optimistic about the economy, at least for now.

originalTitle: US Fed expected to leave rates unchanged next month after soft inflation data
simplifiedContent: The US Federal Reserve is likely to keep interest rates the same at their next meeting in September. This is because the rate of inflation, or how fast prices are rising, has slowed down for the second month in a row. Even though inflation is still a concern, the slower rate means the Fed may not need to raise interest rates right away. However, some signs of ongoing inflation mean that a rate increase is still possible, so the Fed hasn't completely ruled it out. This matters because interest rate changes can affect the overall economy and the stock market.

originalTitle: Corn Jumps as USDA Cuts Yield More Than Expected Amid Heat Waves
simplifiedContent: The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) recently reported that corn crops are not doing as well as expected, mainly because of the hot weather. As a result, the price of corn futures (a way to buy corn at a set price in the future) went up a lot, more than it has since June. This happened because the USDA cut its estimate of how much corn will be produced, and the cut was bigger than most people thought it would be. This is important because corn is a major crop in the US, and changes in its production and price can affect many things. The increase in corn prices could have a big impact on the market and the economy.

originalTitle: US Sells 10-Year Debt at Highest Yields Since Financial Crisis
simplifiedContent: The US government recently sold $42 billion worth of 10-year loans, called Treasuries, to investors. The investors who bought these loans are essentially lending money to the government for 10 years. The government had to offer a high interest rate, known as a yield, to convince investors to lend them money - the highest rate since 2007. This high yield shows that investors are demanding more compensation for lending to the government, likely because they think it's a riskier investment. This sale matters because it indicates how much investors trust the government to pay them back, and how much it costs the government to borrow money.

originalTitle: Oil prices edge up as investors weigh US-Iran talks deadlock against lower demand
simplifiedContent: Oil prices have slightly increased recently. This is happening because investors are considering two main things: the lack of progress in talks between the US and Iran, and the fact that people are using less oil. The deadlock in US-Iran talks might lead to less oil being available, which could increase prices. On the other hand, lower demand for oil could lead to lower prices. It matters because changes in oil prices can affect the overall stock market and the economy.
